author: Rahul kp
title: Call Option
hook: right to buy or right to sell?
simple_words: A call gives the buyer the right to buy; a put gives the right to sell. The buyer pays a premium for this right.

definitions.meaning: Gives the buyer the right, not the duty, to BUY the asset at strike price X on expiry (European) or on/before expiry (American).
Gives the buyer the right, not the duty, to SELL the asset at strike price X on expiry (European) or on/before expiry (American).

key_points: Buyer (holder) pays premium P and has only a ==right==; the writer has the ==obligation== if buyer exercises.
Call is in the money when S > X; put is in the money when S < X (S = spot price at exercise).
Exercise whenever the option is in the money, even if a net loss after premium remains. If out of the money, let it lapse; !!maximum loss of buyer is the premium!!.
Writer's gain is limited to the premium; writer's loss is the buyer's gain, less the premium.

formulas.name: Call buyer payoff
formulas.legend: S = spot price at expiry, X = strike price. Net profit = payoff − premium P.

formulas.name: Put buyer payoff
formulas.legend: S = spot price at expiry, X = strike price. Net profit = payoff − premium P.

insight.text: Writer's payoff is the opposite of the buyer's, plus the premium received.

memory_trick.explanation: You CALL a cab to go UP in price terms: buy now, gain if price rises. You PUT the stock DOWN on the market: sell, gain if price falls.

steps: Compare spot S with strike X
Is it in the money? Exercise
exam_tip: Always state buyer or writer, and say whether the result is before or after the premium. Marks go for this clarity.

doubt.question: Must the buyer always exercise the option?
doubt.answer: No. The buyer has only a right and exercises it only if it is in the money, even if a net loss remains after premium. The writer must perform if the buyer exercises.

mistakes.wrong: Put buyer gains when the spot price rises
mistakes.right: Put buyer gains when spot price falls below strike X (S < X).

mistakes.wrong: Ignoring the premium while stating net profit
mistakes.right: Net profit = payoff − premium for the buyer; for the writer, premium received − payoff.

mistakes.wrong: Buyer exercises only when a net profit is made after premium
mistakes.right: Exercise whenever in the money (call S > X; put S < X); this reduces the loss even if the net result is negative.

Checker 1: Key point 4: 'writer's loss is the buyer's gain, less the premium' is ambiguous. If 'buyer's gain' means the buyer's net profit, taking the premium off again counts it twice. Suggested wording: 'Writer's gain is limited to the premium received; writer's net loss = buyer's payoff − premium = buyer's net profit (for a call writer, this loss can be unlimited).'

Checker 1: Memory trick explanation: 'You CALL a cab to go UP in price terms' is confusing and adds nothing. Suggested wording: 'CALL = buy, so you gain when the price goes UP (S > X); PUT = sell, so you gain when the price goes DOWN (S < X).'
